data.content_ref: inline:The target fails the problem's central demand: it treats the 3-of-26 result merely as a confounded artefact rather than deriving any condition under which a test constrains rather than describes. Its entire 'mechanism' is the confound observation itself, but it never explains what distinguishes the 1-of-9 compile.py loss (under shown-to-fail-first installation) from the 4/4 to 6/7 losses in ordinarily-guarded modules. The problem explicitly asks for the CONDITIONS of constraint and demands an account of the DISTRIBUTION, yet the target's claim reduces to 'this is one repository, one author, one week' and calls the 1-of-9 loss a sign the pattern is a 'local artefact' without explaining why that specific mutation escaped when others did not. It provides no mechanism — no explanation of HOW the acceptance record contaminated the mutation proposals, no formal property that would tell us when a test constrains — and so it answers 'the evidence is too weak' instead of answering the question that was asked.
